newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed at their highest levels for about two months, dragged higher as buoyant German bund futures surged up through the 102.00 level.
The yield on the 10-year benchmark, the 5.75 percent February 2007 state loan, finished at 5.58 percent, a level last seen in mid-March, from 5.64 percent on Friday.
But turnover remained in the doldrums, with Dutch institutions reluctant to commit any of their growing cash holdings to guilder paper until lower levels are seen.
A London-based dealer said international investors also were not interested in the illiquid guilder market.
"It's not that exciting," he said, adding that Spanish bonds offered more excitement and bunds more security.
A trader said the strong rise in bund futures through the afternoon was due to technical, rather than fundamental, factors.
Rabobank International said in its Financial Weekly publication that two-year Dutch bonds looked fair value following the underperformance of Dutch short bonds against Germany in recent months.
It recommended a switch out of the 6.75 percent June 1999 Bund into the 7.50 percent June 1999 Dutch state loan.
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett also said in a report that the yield pick-up in the 1999 area should trigger switching.
The pick-up in this maturity is about 14 basis points.
But traders had not seen any switching into guilders.
"We have seen some people looking at that switch but they're not quite pulling the trigger," said one trader.
A broker however noted "some action" in 1998 and 1999 paper.
Figures awaited this week includes German, U.S. and Dutch inflation, but dealers saw little interest in the Dutch April data on Tuesday, expected to show a 2.0 percent year/year rise.
